subject.title: Discord account-to-agent routing falls back to default agent instead of matching by account name

question: Should Discord multi-account routing add a guarded same-name accountId-to-agent fallback when no explicit binding matches, or should explicit bindings remain the only supported contract?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the change alters security-sensitive fallback semantics for stable Discord routing, session ownership, model/provider selection, and existing users who may rely on default fallback.

options.title: Approve Guarded Fallback
options.body: Route non-default Discord accountIds to an existing same-named configured agent only after explicit binding tiers miss, with distinct diagnostics, docs, focused tests, and live Discord proof.

options.title: Keep Explicit Bindings Only
options.body: Leave runtime routing unchanged and add clearer docs, doctor, or status warnings for Discord accounts that appear intended to bind to same-named agents.

options.title: Repair Linked PR First
options.body: Use the open fork PR only after resolving conflicts, proving the guarded contract, and adding real Discord behavior evidence.

recommendation.title: Approve Guarded Fallback
recommendation.body: Route non-default Discord accountIds to an existing same-named configured agent only after explicit binding tiers miss, with distinct diagnostics, docs, focused tests, and live Discord proof.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent code-history and review signal across shared routing, Discord account/binding routing, and the current fallback contract decision.
